R0032.title: Account Takeover
R0032.definition: Stealing login credentials through trojans, phishing, and other means.
R0032.description: There are two typical types of login credentials: authentication credentials used to log in (primarily username/password, but also one-time passwords, SMS verification codes, biometric features, etc.); and session maintenance credentials used to maintain login state (typically cookies, but also session IDs, nonces, JSON Web Tokens, etc.).
R0032.influence: Grants the attacker persistent account access and operational permissions on the corresponding website or application.

references.title: OWASP Automated Threat: OAT007 Credential Cracking

observables: Login location/device fingerprint changes abruptly, diverging sharply from the historical behavior profile
The session immediately performs sensitive actions (password change, card binding, withdrawal) with no habitual browsing path
A single account shows multiple concurrent sessions from distant locations within a short window

R0032-001.title: Credential Stuffing
R0032-001.definition: Testing the validity of stolen account credentials in the current system through bulk login attempts.
R0032-001.description: Testing a list of stolen authentication credentials against the current system's authentication mechanism to determine whether users have reused the same login credentials. Stolen usernames (usually email addresses) and passwords may have been obtained directly from another application, purchased on criminal markets, or obtained from publicly available breach data dumps. Unlike credential cracking, credential stuffing does not involve any brute force or numerical guessing.
R0032-001.influence: Through unrestricted credential stuffing, attackers may gain access to many users who have reused credentials from other systems, causing losses to those users through further operations.

references.title: OWASP Automated Threat: OAT008 Credential Stuffing

observables: The login endpoint shows large-scale batch attempts using leaked credential libraries, with a spike in failure rate
The same IP/device subnet tests the same password against many different accounts within a short window
Passwords of successfully logged-in accounts overlap heavily with known data-breach credentials

R0032-002.title: Password Spraying
R0032-002.definition: Attempting to log in by trying one or a few common weak passwords against a large number of accounts to obtain valid credentials.
R0032-002.description: Unlike credential brute force (R0032-003) which enumerates passwords for a single account, password spraying fixes one or a few common passwords and tries them against a large number of different user accounts to discover accounts using that weak password. This approach avoids triggering account lockout mechanisms that would result from multiple failed attempts on a single account.
R0032-002.influence: Through unrestricted credential attacks, attackers may gain access to users with weak passwords on the current system, causing losses through further operations.

references.title: OWASP Automated Threat: OAT007 Credential Cracking

observables: The login endpoint shows a large number of accounts being tried against the same weak password, with low per-account failure counts but broad account coverage
The same IP/device attempts logins against large numbers of different accounts within a short window, deliberately staying below the account-lockout threshold
Successfully logged-in accounts use common weak passwords (e.g., 123456, qwerty), heavily overlapping with weak-password dictionaries

R0032-003.title: Credential Brute Force
R0032-003.definition: Attempting to log in by brute-forcing a list of possible passwords for a specific account to obtain valid credentials.
R0032-003.description: Using brute force, dictionary (word list), and guessing attacks against the application's authentication process to identify the weak credentials used by a specific account — for example, enumerating a user's password.
R0032-003.influence: After gaining full control of the target account, attackers can steal funds, virtual assets, and private data, and launch secondary phishing, fraud, or bulk account-farming operations; the abnormal login traffic consumes server resources and triggers account lockouts that degrade login experience for legitimate users, and account takeover can spread laterally to linked business platforms, causing compounding losses.

references.title: OWASP Automated Threat: OAT007 Credential Cracking

observables: A single account shows a large number of login failures within a short window, with the failure cause concentrated on incorrect password
The password field in login requests matches common dictionaries or rainbow tables, exhibiting enumeration characteristics
The same IP/device continuously tries different passwords against a single account, triggering account lockout or rate limiting

R0032-004.title: Verification Code Brute Force
R0032-004.definition: Attempting to log in by brute-forcing verification codes to obtain valid credentials.
R0032-004.description: Verification code brute force risk refers to attackers attempting to break verification codes by continuously trying various possibilities to gain access to a system or account. Causes include: weak verification code design; lack of security protections such as frequently changing codes or lockout mechanisms; reuse of the same verification code across multiple locations; and inadequate verification code generation algorithms.
R0032-004.influence: Defeats verification-code protections, allowing attackers to take over accounts, bypass login checks, or trigger subsequent fraud operations.

observables: The verification code validation endpoint is hit at high frequency within a short window, trying a different verification code value on each attempt
The failure count for a single account's verification code surges, exhibiting enumeration characteristics
Endpoints using weak verification codes (4-digit numeric, no expiry, no attempt limit) are enumerated in bulk, with an anomalous success rate
